articleBody:
Getting ready for a family room addition takes more than picking paint colors. Preparing your property and paperwork beforehand keeps the construction schedule moving smoothly and prevents unexpected site delays.

- [ ] Current boundary survey — confirms exact setback lines, lot coverage allowances, and utility easements before design work starts.
- [ ] Detailed functional layout sketch — identifies planned furniture groupings, TV placement, and exterior door openings for natural foot traffic.
- [ ] HVAC system capacity evaluation — checks whether your current heating and cooling unit can handle the additional conditioned air volume.
- [ ] Electrical panel load inspection — verifies available breaker slots for new lighting, ceiling fans, and home entertainment circuits.
- [ ] Underground utility marking request — ensures water lines, electrical feeds, and irrigation pipes are flagged before digging the foundation.
- [ ] Roofline elevation assessment — determines how new valley flashing and shingles will tie into your existing roof plane without causing leaks.
- [ ] Written contractor scope of work — spells out construction materials, structural drawings, payment schedules, and permit responsibilities clearly.
- [ ] Staging area plan for materials — establishes where concrete trucks, framing lumber, and waste dumpsters will sit on your driveway or lawn.

How to use this checklist
Go through these items during your initial planning phase before signing off on final construction drawings. Having clear answers for each item protects your budget and prevents mid-build surprises once construction crews arrive on site.
